definitions.explanation: An exclamation used when one realizes a mistake has been made or something has gone wrong. Expresses regret or dismay at something that has already happened.

examples.japanese: しまった、{鍵|かぎ}をかけ{忘|わす}れた。
examples.english: Darn it, I forgot to lock the door.

examples.japanese: しまった、{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れてしまった。
examples.english: Oh no, I missed the train.

notes:
Derived from the past tense of {仕舞|しま}う (to finish/put away), but used independently as an interjection. The literal sense is that something undesirable has been completed and cannot be undone.

Used when reacting to one's own mistakes or oversights. Can be said aloud or as an internal thought.

RELATED WORDS:
- しまった！ — standard expression of regret
- しまったな — softer, more reflective (male speech)
- やってしまった — I've done it (expressing regret about a completed action)

cross_references.label: I messed up, I screwed up
